### Warranty Coverage
**Glass Warranty**: 
The warranty for the 100 Series promises that your window glass will be free from defects starting at the time of purchase for a period of 20 years from the time of purchase


**Components Warranty**: 
Everything but the noted exclusions is covered for a period of 10 years from the time of purchase
 (this includes items such as the screen, lifts, weatherstripping, balance systems, sash, frame, etc.)

**Transferability**: 
That means that all parts of the protection transfer to the new homeowner if you sell your house before the plan expires


**Labor**: 
Replacement part (labor for installation is not included)
 - NOT INCLUDED in warranty coverage

**Warranty Limitations**: 
Note in the paragraph above, they say you give up your right to be involved in a class action suit or to have a jury trial. ## 4. RED FINDINGS

### Active Recall (February 2026)


This recall involves window opening control devices sold individually as kits or as factory-installed accessories and applied to 100 Series casement windows that were manufactured prior to November 19, 2025. Recall Date: February 26, 2026 · Units: About 91,000
. 
The window opening control devices can break or detach after accidental or other impact, allowing the window to be opened, posing fall and serious injury hazards


**IMPORTANT NOTE**: This recall affects casement windows with opening control devices, NOT the double-hung configuration reviewed here.

### Consumer Complaint Patterns

**Quality Control Concerns**: 
By the way, I've heard from one general contractor that he no longer recommends Andersen windows due to poor QC over past few years. He says he actually asks buyers to sign an acknowledgement if they insist on Andersen that the windows will not be perfect like in the past
 **INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW** - Quality control issues are product manufacturing concerns.

**Window Operation Issues**: 
Overall a good window but operating window seems very loose if you push up on any side when opened you can visually see how crooked it looks! While opening window it is very unstable. Not recommend it. Had high expectation from Anderson brand
 **INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM** - Could be installation or product quality related.

**Manufacturing Defects**: 
Had Andersen Series 100 windows (recommended for high heat areas) installed in my new home. Three of the windows now have extensive cracks on the sashes, and the glazing beads have fallen off. I have contacted Andersen numerous times. They sent out a field rep and refused to take care of the problem
 **INSTALL-CONFOUND: LOW** - Hardware failures are product issues.

**Thermal Performance Issues**: 
We built a new home in February 2024, in which the builder installed Andersen 100 series windows. From the first day we moved in, we experienced extreme temperature variations between rooms. In summer with outside temperatures over 90, some rooms were 80 degrees. The thermostat remains set at 70 degrees. After a thorough investigation with an infrared temperature gun and thermometers, the windows turned out to be the source of the problem
 **INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM** - Mix of installation and manufacturing issues.

**Critical**:
